turns.response_html: If you can't find a replacement pin, you might be able to use a small bolt and nut as a temporary fix. Just make sure it's the right size and won't interfere with the door closing. Do you have any other questions about fixing the handle?

turns.prompt_text: are there any household items or materials that could be used in the meantime
turns.response_html:
You're looking for a quick and simple fix, which is a great idea for a temporary solution. While it's always best to use the correct part, some household items can work in a pinch.

A few things you could try:

  • A paperclip: A large, sturdy paperclip can often be bent and inserted to act as a pin. This is a common temporary fix, but be aware that it might not be very durable and could break with repeated use.
  • A small nail or screw: If you have a very small nail or screw that fits snugly, it can work. Just make sure it's not so long that it will get in the way of the handle's movement or the door's function.
  • A cotter pin: If you happen to have one of these in a toolbox or junk drawer, it's a perfect fit for this kind of job. They're designed to hold things in place and are much stronger than a paperclip.

For any of these fixes, you want to make sure the item you use is a good fit and won't fall out or cause damage.
